scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let J > 0, and let U satisfy the finite-range and symmetry assumptions above. There is λ0 = λ0(J, U) > 0 such that for every |λ| < λ0 there is a positive inverse temperature βc = βc(J, U, λ), independent of domains and boundary data, with βc(J, U, 0) = β0 := log(1 + √ 2) 2J , for which the following holds. Let D be any bounded Jordan domain, let a, b be distinct boundary points, and let δn ↓ 0. For each n, choose a domain Ωn, marks and stubs ξn, and an admissible exterior contour Po,n as above. Suppose there are boundary homeomorphisms ϕn : ∂D −→ ∂(δnDΩn ) such that sup z∈∂D |ϕn(z) − z| −→ 0, ϕn(a) = δnfin,n, ϕn(b) = δnfout,n. If Pn has law µ ξn,Po,n Ωn,βc,λ, then δnγ(Pn) converges in distribution, in the metric (1.2), to chordal SLE3 in D from a to b.
